newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah, ringgit down ahead holiday.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah, ringgit down ahead holiday.

text.p: * Indonesian rupiah eases despite tight liquidity as players go long dollars ahead of a holiday.
* Malaysian ringgit also hit by pre-holiday dollar covering and ringgit/Singapore dollar liquidation.
* Thai baht shows weak bias amid easier liquidity, stock market sell-off.
* Singapore dollar off lows on ringgit/Sing sales.
The Indonesian rupiah and Malaysian ringgit came under pressure despite weakness in the dollar/majors on Wednesday as players covered their dollar positions ahead of a holiday in both centres.
Jakarta dealers said operators moved to cover positions and some went long on dollars because of Thursday's public holiday, driving the dollar up despite a tight rupiah market.
"But I think the dollar appears to be toppish at the 2,429.0 level for now," a U.S. bank dealer said. The rate was likely to range between 2,427 and 2,429 for the day, he added.
Dealers said the market showed no immediate response to news of a slight increase in April inflation and a healthy trade surplus for February.
They said the focus remained on liquidity and the campaign for general elections on May 29.
Spot rupiah, due May 12, was at 2,428.00/29.00 at 0440 GMT against an opening of 2,425.5/26.5.
In Malaysia, the ringgit was hit by continued commercial dollar demand as well as long liquidation of the ringgit/Singapore dollar cross.
"There's dollar buying ahead of the holiday and also continued selling of the ringgit/Sing cross on any rallies," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.
He said dollar/ringgit looked set for a target of 2.5150.
The ringgit was at 2.5123/33 to the dollar at 0440 GMT against 2.5073/80 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
"Ringgit/Sing should head for much lower areas. I wouldn't be surprised if we break the 0.5700 level, but not today," another Singapore-based dealer said.
Ringgit/Sing was quoted at 0.5754/60 at 0440 GMT against its opening 0.5775.
Dealers said the market was also nervous over reports that Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad would be taking a holiday of more than a month.
Mahathir, who keeps a full schedule, seldom takes holidays of longer than a few weeks. During his absence Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is expected to step in.
The Singapore dollar benefited from its neighbour's weakened tone but remained well confined within its recent range of 1.4430-1.4480 against the U.S. dollar.
In Thailand, the baht was little changed at midday after edging up a notch in line with the weaker/dollar majors in early trade.
Dealers said the Thai unit showed a downside bias amid ample liquidity and a sell-off on the stock market.

The baht was quoted at 26.082/26.087 to the dollar at 0440 GMT against 26.085/26.089 late Tuesday. The Bank of Thailand fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate on Wednesday at 26.06 baht against 26.10 on Tuesday.
"The baht was traded at the ceiling as banks bought actively...perhaps to cover positions," a foreign bank dealer in Bangkok said.
The interbank rate softened early as commercial banks, which had already met their reserve requirements, offered aggressively in the market, dealers said.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anchalee Koetswang in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
